title: Uddhav Thackeray calls for regime change at Shiv Sena UBT Dussehra rally
seoTitle: Mumbai Dussehra rally calls for regime change

tea.why: Protesters and party leaders are angry over alleged vote theft, deleted electoral rolls, and government crackdowns on youth.
tea.want: Protesters and opposition leaders are demanding justice and a change in the central government regime.
tea.changed: Oct 20, 2026: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray addressed the annual Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park, supporting anti-government protests.

summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray addressed the party's annual Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Mumbai on October 20, 2026, openly stating that his party supports ongoing anti-government protests with the objective of bringing about a regime change. Speaking to party workers at the 60th anniversary of the rally, Thackeray defended the youths participating in street demonstrations, rejecting claims that they were urban naxalites and calling them revolutionaries seeking their rights. He criticised authorities over alleged vote theft, discrepancies in electoral rolls, and police brutality against protesters. While no specific official response to the rally was documented, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde announced foodgrain distribution for farmers during the event.
demands: Address electoral roll discrepancies and vote theft
Bring about a government regime change
response: Maharashtra Deputy CM Eknath Shinde announced 100 tonnes of foodgrains for farmers at the Shiv Sena Dussehra rally. No direct official response from the central government was reported in the sources.

updates.text: Shiv Sena (UBT) held its 60th annual Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, featuring speeches calling for a regime change.
